explanation: Deserts are typically located at latitudes of approximately 30° in both the Northern and Southern Hemispheres, covering nearly 30% of the Earth's total land surface. They are formed by descending dry atmospheric winds that lack moisture. Deserts receive less than 25 cm of annual rainfall and experience large temperature fluctuations between day and night. Resident plants and animals have evolved specialized adaptations to conserve water.
